lines.text: Remember when summer felt like forever? Now whole years disappear.
One idea, from 1877, is the proportional theory.
When you're five, one year is a fifth of your entire life.
When you're fifty, it's just one fiftieth.
The other big idea is novelty.
As a kid, everything is new, so your brain records lots of detailed memories.
As adults, routine days blur together. Fewer new memories make the time feel shorter looking back.
William James wrote that the years grow hollow and collapse.

visual.text: The years grow hollow and collapse

lines.text: So if you want a year to feel longer, fill it with new things.

sources.claim: Proportional (ratio) theory from 1877; novelty explanation from William James, Principles of Psychology (1890): 'the years grow hollow and collapse'
